contract.reader: An engineer or student who knows difference equations, impulse responses and BIBO stability from the first entry and wants to analyze a recursive system without summing infinite series
contract.problem: Deciding from a difference equation whether a system is stable, how its response decays and which frequencies it passes or blocks
contract.outcome: Write a transfer function from a difference equation, find poles and zeros, invert by partial fractions, test stability (unit circle, stability triangle), map s-plane poles to the z-plane and place poles and zeros by hand for a notch filter
contract.contribution: One path from the z-transform to a working notch design, with every step tied back to the first entry and forward to the filter-design and digital-control entries, and the numbers reproduced by two runnable scripts
contract.evidence: Derivations in the text; two Python scripts with their real output; five worked exercises; Jury (1964), Oppenheim and Schafer (2010), Proakis and Manolakis (2007)
contract.limitations: Causal sequences only; no bilateral transform, no residue or contour inversion; no figure of a pole-zero plot or of a frequency response

findings.problem: The article explains the pole-zero plot and reads the gain geometrically from distances in it, but shows no plot; the 5.3 notch is given only as coefficients and a table of gains.
findings.whyItMatters: The geometric reading is the main idea of Section 5 and the design method of 5.3; a reader new to it must construct the picture alone.
findings.action: Add one generated figure for the 5.3 notch: pole-zero plot with the unit circle beside its magnitude response 0 to 500 Hz, from the article's formulas, with a caption saying what to notice.
findings.acceptance: On new captures the figure appears in 5.3, readable at 1280 and 360 px and in dark mode, with a null at 50 Hz and about 0.70 at 47 and 53 Hz.

findings.problem: At 360 px the 1.2 equation ends before its result 1/(1 - az^-1) and ROC |z| > |a|; the transform table's ROC column and the 2.1 and 2.2 right-hand sides are hidden (scroll without cue).
findings.whyItMatters: A phone reader sees the 1.2 equation without the result and region of convergence the section establishes.
findings.action: Split the 1.2 equation over two lines and the 2.1 and 2.2 equations at their equals signs (aligned blocks); the table needs the site-level scroll cue.
findings.acceptance: At 360 px the 1.2 result with its ROC and the full right-hand sides of the 2.1 and 2.2 equations are visible without sideways scrolling.

findings.problem: The node label reads 'H(e^jω)' with a literal caret, and the diagram has no caption.
findings.whyItMatters: Plain-text notation in a page that typesets every other expression; polish.
findings.action: Typeset the exponent (HTML superscript in the Mermaid label) and add a one-line caption.
findings.acceptance: On new captures the label shows a superscript exponent and the diagram has a caption.
